items.action: Patch or remove affected Cisco Expressway, vCenter, Apache Roller and SAP NetWeaver Portal systems today, and hunt for prior compromise before patching.
items.details: The vCenter bypass was reportedly exploited by the China-linked group Armory Castle. Cisco's fix is Expressway X15.5.20 or later; no workarounds exist for the Expressway flaw.
items.summary: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalog on Nov 20 with a federal patch deadline of today, Nov 23: Cisco Expressway hard-coded credentials (CVE-2026-76466, CVSS 9.8), VMware vCenter authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8), Apache Roller deserialization (CVE-2026-129448, CVSS 9.8) and SAP NetWeaver Portal (CVE-2025-42884, CVSS 6.5).
items.title: CISA KEV deadline today: Cisco, VMware, Apache and SAP flaws

items.action: Install the stable security firmware for your exact model, run both the official process check and the community detection tool GL.iNet links to, and factory-reset any device showing either indicator.
items.details: RemoteToHome Consulting reported the older backdoor on 47 of 183 routers it checked since Saturday. It survives firmware updates that keep settings, so the official 'crond -i /tmp/.log' check alone is not sufficient.
items.summary: GL.iNet updated its GoodCloud incident notice on Nov 23 with stable security firmware for routers and KVMs after attackers exploited its cloud remote-management service to plant malware. Separately, owners checking devices found an older backdoor, dating back to September 2025 on some routers, that GL.iNet's official check does not detect.
items.title: GL.iNet fallout widens: stable firmware out, second older backdoor found

items.action: Upgrade Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or your distro's fixed package everywhere it runs — including inside containers — and check WordPress/media-processing hosts that invoke it.
items.details: Research published Nov 17 by Paulos Yibelo and pwn.ai; these are research demonstrations, not confirmed in-the-wild attacks. Artifex fixed the flaw in Ghostscript 10.08.0.
items.summary: A use-after-free flaw in Ghostscript's -dSAFER sandbox (CVE-2026-125396, CVSS 8.5) lets a booby-trapped uploaded file run commands on servers that process PDFs or images; researchers demonstrated it against WordPress, Roundcube webmail and Linux print servers.
items.title: Ghostscript 'Upload2Shell' sandbox escape — CVE-2026-125396

items.action: Spot customers: reissue API and refresh tokens, download fresh kubeconfigs, rotate every credential stored in cluster Secrets, and review downstream logs back to Nov 17.
items.details: Rackspace learned of the intrusion Nov 18 from a customer report, revoked tokens and sessions, removed unauthorized pods and restored service Nov 21. IOCs shared: IP 23.224.79.106, range 23.224.0.0/15, and pod/object prefixes i1, glm- and probe. Customer count and whether data was copied out remain undisclosed.
items.summary: Rackspace warned customers that on Nov 17 an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of its Spot Kubernetes platform for about 22 hours, creating pods and reading Kubernetes Secrets, Spot API tokens and refresh tokens in some customer clusters.
items.title: Rackspace Spot breach: attackers read customer Kubernetes secrets

items.action: Treat as an unverified claim: watch for a Samsung statement and sample data before acting, and do not cite the 1TB figure as confirmed.
items.details: The claims were reported by ThreatMon on Nov 22. A leak-site listing alone does not establish that data was stolen or which Samsung entity, if any, was involved. This is separate from Samsung's confirmed Nov 20 third-party advertising-vendor breach.
items.summary: On Nov 22 the HYFLOCK ransomware group claimed Samsung Group as a victim, alleging about 1TB of data stolen; Qilin separately listed Invicta Watch Group. Neither claim is independently confirmed and no Samsung statement on this claim has been reported.
items.title: HYFLOCK claims 1TB Samsung Group breach; Qilin lists Invicta (both unverified)

items.action: Affected cardholders should expect direct notification and credit-monitoring offers; security teams should review vendor-held marketing data as an exposure surface.
items.details: Visa said a vendor in Asia-Pacific was involved, affecting about 6,000 premium customers; Mastercard confirmed limited information for a subset of cardholders in one benefit program. n0n named 59 organizations in the same campaign.
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirmed that third-party vendors serving them were hit after the n0n ransomware gang listed them on Nov 16. Exposed data was marketing/contact data — including about 16,000 JPMorgan Reserve customer email addresses — with no card numbers affected and core systems untouched, the companies said.
items.title: n0n vendor breach: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard confirm limited exposure

items.action: Never install banking apps sent via WhatsApp or Telegram; banks distribute apps only through official app stores. Report APK fraud on the 1930 helpline or the NCRP portal.
items.details: Police linked the accused to 2,080 NCRP complaints and examined 32 malicious APKs. The apps, pushed with KYC, life-certificate and credit-limit lures aimed mainly at senior citizens, harvested banking credentials, OTPs, SMS and call records; proceeds were laundered through discounted e-commerce coupons sold on Telegram. APK fraud complaints in Delhi fell over 48% in the week after the raids.
items.summary: Delhi Police arrested 22 people across Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Bihar in a Nov 11–15 operation against 11 syndicates that allegedly used fake banking APKs sent over WhatsApp to dupe over 22,000 people of more than Rs 20 crore.
items.title: Delhi Police bust fake-APK fraud ring: 22 arrested, 22,139 victims

items.action: Government and enterprise payment portals need independent security review of third-party processors, and banks should flag new mule-account patterns on large transfers.
items.details: Police said the gang used fake web addresses to infiltrate the payment site and routed funds through thousands of money-mule accounts, converting proceeds to cryptocurrency. Three special task forces have been sent to other states to track the mule network; account holders were allegedly paid a 10% commission.
items.summary: Chennai cyber crime police said fraudsters siphoned about Rs 22 crore from a private bank account held in the name of the Tamil Nadu Rural Development Department by exploiting flaws in a third-party payment portal; nine people have been arrested.
items.title: Rs 22 crore siphoned from Tamil Nadu Rural Development Dept account; 9 held

items.action: Treat as unverified claims pending company statements; partners and clients of either firm should watch for official disclosure before changing posture.
items.details: QPulse, citing Ransomware.live and HudsonRock infostealer data for the Persistent listing, reports an estimated initial attack date of Nov 9. Leak-site claims are the group's own assertions, not confirmed breaches.
items.summary: The Incransom ransomware group listed persistent.com on Nov 22 and Cybage Software on Nov 22–23 as alleged victims on its leak site. Neither claim has been independently verified and neither company had issued a public statement in the reporting.
items.title: Incransom claims Indian IT firms Persistent and Cybage (unverified)

subtitle: Monday, November 23 — CISA's patch deadline lands today, GL.iNet fallout widens, and Delhi Police bust a 22,000-victim APK fraud ring.
title: Morning Cybersecurity Digest
